summary: After Ryan Blaney won the NASCAR Cup Series championship at Phoenix in a Ford Mustang, Ford Performance global director Mark Rushbrook said winning is the basis of Ford's marketing and that Ford sells more F-150s than Mustangs to NASCAR fans. The article also covers how Roger Penske calmed Blaney during the closing laps, when he was frustrated with Ross Chastain.
one_line: Ford's Mark Rushbrook says NASCAR success sells more F-150s than Mustangs, after Ryan Blaney's Phoenix title and Roger Penske's calming radio advice.
key_facts: Ryan Blaney won his first-ever NASCAR Cup Series championship at Phoenix in a Ford Mustang.
Blaney held off late challenges from Chevrolet drivers Kyle Larson and William Byron.
Ford made a clean sweep of the Truck, Xfinity, and Cup Series championships.
Mark Rushbrook, Global Director for Ford Performance, said: "winning is everything for us, just as a point of pride."
Rushbrook said success on the racetrack is "the basis for successful marketing programs" and gives Ford credibility with fans.
Rushbrook said: "we certainly sell Mustangs because of it. But we sell more F-150s to NASCAR fans."
Ben Rhodes won his second Truck Series championship on Friday in a Ford F-150.
The seventh generation Mustang is sold globally and races in Australia Supercars, Mustang GT3, Mustang GT4, and Dark Horse R with a Spec Challenge.
In the closing laps, Blaney was racing Ross Chastain for the lead, and Chastain blocked him multiple times.
Blaney made contact with Chastain out of frustration, as he admitted.
Team owner Roger Penske, called "The Captain," reminded Blaney he was racing the HMS duo, not Chastain.
Blaney said: "There is no secret that I can snap on the radio. That's been my whole life."
